ai.claude: This newsletter runs on exactly this kind of memory: short notes on what broke in earlier runs are what keep each Daily from repeating old mistakes. The lesson from the Pokémon test is that fewer, better notes beat a big pile of them, which is true for people as well.
ai.fact: Anthropic published research on how Claude agents use idle time to check the notes they keep as files against logs of past work, fixing errors and reorganising what they remember. It says newer models are much better at judging what to save, and that explaining why memory matters works better than rules on what to write; in a Pokémon test, Fable 5 earned four badges with 10 memory files while the older Sonnet 3.7 earned one with 413, The Rundown AI reports.

austrian.claude: An Austrian would call the miners' move healthy: prices are telling them that a megawatt earns more renting to an AI lab than hashing, and capital follows. The counter-argument is that the AI side of that price is itself inflated by cheap funding, so miners may be swapping a hard asset for a lease tied to the boom that just sold off. On Tether the school's answer is simple: unaudited reserves deserve no trust.
austrian.fact: Riot Platforms cut its bitcoin from 11,380 to 2,418 coins in the third quarter, mostly to fund data centres, and signed a 15-year lease of its 910-megawatt Corsicana, Texas campus to an AI lab worth about $28bn, Bitcoin Treasuries reports; Keel Infrastructure (formerly Bitfarms) sold all its bitcoin for the same reason. Tether's CEO Paolo Ardoino said in Lugano the company owns about 150,000 BTC, while its latest reserve attestation shows about 100,000.

opinion.text: the extra 50,000 coins are a claim, not a disclosure, until Tether says where they sit and who holds them.

mainstream.claude: Both incumbents who missed out sit on the political flanks, so the runoff is a test of whether Fribourg's centre is willing to keep a left-right balance in its seven-seat government.
mainstream.fact: In the first round of Fribourg's cantonal government election, FDP incumbents Romain Collaud and Didier Castella and Mitte's Marie-France Roth Pasquier won their seats outright, SRF reports. SVP minister Philippe Demierre (37,095 votes) and Green minister Sylvie Bonvin-Sansonnens (32,617) fell short of the absolute majority, and the remaining four seats go to a second round on 29 November.

top.claude: The bigger market risk is not this week's share price but policy: a Democratic Congress now has a concrete case for tighter chip controls and closer vetting of resellers in Southeast Asia, which would hit Nvidia's sales more than any board review.
top.fact: Nvidia's board said on Sunday that a committee of independent directors with outside lawyers will review whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort; Huang stays CEO, and the board says it has no reason to believe national-security or company secrets were compromised. In a letter to staff Huang admitted an extramarital affair and apologised. Al Jazeera and Euronews report the woman worked for Megaspeed, a Singapore firm that bought about $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment and that US officials suspect of routing chips to China; China denies the spying claims. House Republicans have asked Huang to brief Congress.

opinion.text: modern espionage is about a mosaic of small insights, not one stolen blueprint, so asking only whether a secret leaked misses whether the affair shaped how Nvidia vetted buyers and lobbied on export controls.

top.claude: Europe's worry is a deal agreed over Kyiv's head; being in the room in Abu Dhabi is the only way to avoid that, which is why Barrot's announcement matters more than the G7 statement that will follow.
top.fact: US, Russian and Ukrainian officials meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday; US envoy Steve Witkoff says the agenda covers security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe's post-war security set-up and reconstruction, Semafor reports. French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Europeans will join the talks, Euronews reports, and G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris this week to press for a bigger European role.

opinion.text: as long as the White House accepts small gestures instead of real concessions, Putin will not change course.

top.claude: Declaring victory while squeezing harder is a classic way to set up a deal on your own terms; the risk is that Tehran, which claims credit for the Republicans' midterm losses, reads US politics as a reason to wait.
top.fact: President Trump said the US has won the war and that the land blockade of Iran is now in effect, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio reported no progress in talks, Euronews and Al Jazeera report. Trump also said further US strikes were highly unlikely, and Iran said negotiations were paused after the US midterms, according to Semafor. Brent stayed near $98 a barrel, about 17% lower than a week ago.

top.claude: This is what a bank run looks like when one app holds most of a country's young savers: the run was fast, and the political damage came even faster than the losses can be counted.
top.fact: Ueno, Paraguay's largest digital bank, collapsed amid allegations of insider lending and ties to the ruling Colorado party, cutting off about half the population from their funds, Semafor reports. Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest, SRF reports, and Euronews reports Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in on 7 November after the impeachment.

top.fact: The UN climate summit opened on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, with Australia chairing the negotiations, Semafor and International Intrigue report. Euronews reports European governments are scrambling for more fossil fuels even as they push for climate ambition, and swissinfo reports Switzerland's priority is defending existing commitments.

opinion.text: petrostate resistance, US absence and indifference from big emitters make a major breakthrough highly unlikely.
